security: No current LTS lockdown, kernel-file loading or io_uring permission hook is removed. Generic lockdown audit/reasons are retained, while obsolete SELinux lockdown enforcement stays absent as in LTS. SDK SECURITY_LOCKDOWN_LSM is disabled. memfd_file introduces policy-selected distinct labels and execution permissions; successful authorization depends on selected policy, and it does not imply all memfd execution is denied. Native NNP/nosuid and process-transition safeguards remain. Capability-disabled SELinux returns without relabeling memfd, as ACK specifies. Other LSM hooks still run through the native dispatcher.
uncertainty: The examined pinned policy_capabilities file has no memfd_class directive, despite current memfd_file rules and libsepol support. Final SDK assembled policy activation was not established. Retain current generic Android runtime/policy interface conservatively; do not claim a booted policy or treat a missing search result as proof of dispensability.
